Alacritty's configuration file uses the TOML format.
Alacritty can be installed by using various package managers on Linux, BSD, macOS and Windows.
cargo build --release
cargo install alacritty
In vi mode the search is bound to / for forward and ? for backward search.
you can start a selection using v and copy it using y
After making a selection, you can use the right mouse button to expand it.
Colors are specified using their hexadecimal values with a # prefix: #RRGGBB.
cargo build --release --no-default-features --features=wayland
This means you won't find things like tabs or splits (which are best left to a window manager or terminal multiplexer)

By default you can start a selection using v and copy it using y. All selection modes that are available with the mouse can be accessed from vi mode, including the semantic (Alt v), line (Shift v) and block selection (Ctrl v).
Search allows you to find anything in Alacritty's scrollback buffer. You can search forward using Ctrl Shift f (Command f on macOS) and backward using Ctrl Shift b (Command b on macOS).
The `SearchStart` and `SearchEnd` keybinding actions can be bound if you're looking for a way to jump to the start or the end of a match.

After making a selection, you can use the right mouse button to expand it. Double-clicking will expand the selection semantically, while triple-clicking will perform line selection. If you hold Ctrl while expanding the selection, it will switch to the block selection mode.
You can open URLs with your mouse by clicking on them. The modifiers required to be held and program which should open the URL can be setup in the configuration file.
Colors are specified using their hexadecimal values with a _#_ prefix: _#RRGGBB_.
Request compositor to blur content behind transparent windows.
Blank space added around the window in pixels. This padding is scaled by DPI and the specified value is always added at both opposing sides.
Offset is the extra space around each character. _y_ can be thought of as modifying the line spacing, and _x_ as modifying the letter spacing.

The software is considered to be at a **beta** level of readiness; there are
a few missing features and bugs to be fixed, but it is already used by many as
a daily driver.
Alacritty uses vtebench to quantify terminal emulator throughput and manages to consistently score better than the competition using it.
The state of terminal emulators on macOS is particularly bad, at least when it comes to speed. Alacritty fills a void for folks that want no-frills fast terminal emulation.
It really is the fastest one I ever used. Font rendering is great.
find /Applications results: Hyper crashed, iTerm2 1:28, Terminal 0:20... Alacritty was surprisingly good, very impressive stuff.
I really disagree with the author's definition of minimal. I need scrollback, tabs, and monitor for activity/silence - I can't really use this until he reconsiders.
Nice, but: thread 'pty reader' panicked at 'index out of bounds'... or thread 'pty reader' panicked at 'cursor fell off grid'.
I understand the point of view of the author, but at the same time I appreciate how simple and not bloated Alacritty is, unlike great software terribly bloated with edge-case features.
I used to use kitty, but its CPU usage was on the higher side. I tried alacritty but the lack of tabs was a deal-breaker, so I switched to Wezterm instead.
Ah! The 'classic' ligature issue. Have been following that for a while. Kind of given up hope that there will ever be any support for it.
I really enjoy Alacritty and use it every day. The performance is amazing!
Alacritty doesn't do well with modifier keys and a lot of keyboard shortcuts don't work in neovim by default. I recommend using foot instead.
kitty has a problem with garbled unicode sequences hanging for a minute or two on invalid sequences; I switched to alacritty because it doesn't have this problem.
I gave it a shot on Windows with wsl2. Hit weird config gotchas since they switched to toml, couldn't get tmux/neovim shortcuts to work, gave up and went back to Windows Terminal.
Been using alacritty for few years but moved to wezterm recently.
it also opens faster [than kitty], which is important for me, as I use a tiling window manager and open/close terminals fairly often instead of using something like tmux.
